Productivity of Transcripts and Genes

Source: R/productivity.R
productivity.Rd

The biotype split used by the workflow (protein coding versus retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay, ...) is a proxy. These functions make productivity a computed, graded property of every transcript and summarise it per gene:

  • transcript_productivity() classifies each assayed transcript as "productive" (complete ORF, no predicted NMD, same ORF as the canonical isoform), "altered_productive" (complete ORF, no NMD, but a different ORF than the canonical isoform: alternative start, in-frame change, frameshift or stop in novel sequence), "unproductive" (no ORF, premature stop codon by the 50-nt rule, no stop codon, an unproductive biotype such as nonsense_mediated_decay, retained_intron, protein_coding_CDS_not_defined, or a longest ORF without coding potential), "noncoding" (transcripts of genes without any coding isoform) or "uncertain" (incomplete CDS annotation without a premature stop, a credible ORF unrelated to the canonical one, FANTOM uncertain_coding). The reason column explains each call and source tells whether it came from the sequence ("sequence", when the annotation has transcript sequences, see extract_transcript_sequences() and transcript_orfs()), the annotation ("annotation") or external evidence ("evidence"). Evidence columns take precedence, in this order: a productivity_evidence column added with add_annotation_columns(), a validated NMD exon (add_nmd_exons()), a Ribo-seq ORF matching the transcript's ORF (add_riboseq_orfs()), an APPRIS principal isoform (add_appris()).

  • productive_fraction() is the share of a gene's expression carried by productive (and altered productive) isoforms, per sample or per group, with the difference between the last and the first group level. A gene whose expression is flat while its productive fraction drops is a post-transcriptional regulation call that gene-level differential expression misses. With inferential replicates (inf_reps, Salmon bootstraps or Gibbs samples) it reports the uncertainty of each fraction, and with a reference (gtex_reference()) the difference to the healthy-tissue baseline.

  • productivity_fractions() splits the gene's expression over all productivity classes and, for unproductive isoforms, over the mechanism (nmd, retained_intron, no_orf, non_stop, other).

  • test_productive_fraction() tests the change in productive fraction between two groups on counts, with a quasi-binomial model per gene (pooled proportions per group, Pearson over-dispersion, t test on the log odds ratio, BH adjustment).

  • run_productivity_enrichment() ranks genes by the change in productive fraction between two groups and runs gene set enrichment (fgsea) on gene symbols, which captures regulated unproductive splicing (AS-NMD) directly.

  • poison_exons() lists exons that occur only in unproductive isoforms of genes that also have productive isoforms and that do not overlap any exon of a productive isoform (cassette poison / NMD exons, as opposed to retained introns or alternative splice sites); plot_genomic_context() outlines them with highlight_poison_exons.

  • benchmark_productivity() measures the rules against the annotation biotypes: recall of nonsense_mediated_decay and retained_intron transcripts by the sequence/structure rules alone, and the share of protein_coding and canonical transcripts called productive.

  • productivity_palette() gives colours for the classes.

Usage

productivity_palette()

transcript_productivity(
  self,
  gene_name = NULL,
  nmd_rule = 50,
  use_biotype = TRUE,
  use_sequence = TRUE,
  use_evidence = TRUE,
  coding_cutoff = 0.364,
  ...
)

productive_fraction(
  self,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "abundance",
  include_altered = TRUE,
  as_matrix = FALSE,
  gene_name = NULL,
  min_expr = 0,
  inf_reps = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  ...
)

productivity_fractions(
  self,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "abundance",
  min_expr = 0,
  gene_name = NULL,
  ...
)

test_productive_fraction(
  self,
  group,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "counts",
  include_altered = TRUE,
  min_expr = 0,
  gene_name = NULL,
  ...
)

run_productivity_enrichment(
  self,
  genesets_list,
  group,
  levels = NULL,
  assay = "abundance",
  min_size = 15,
  max_size = 500,
  ...
)

poison_exons(self, gene_name = NULL, ...)

benchmark_productivity(self, nmd_rule = 50, use_sequence = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment.

gene_name

Optional genes (names or IDs) to restrict the result to.

nmd_rule

Distance (nt) from the stop codon to the last junction above which NMD is predicted; default 50.

use_biotype

Logical, also use unproductive biotypes and FANTOM coding status (default TRUE).

use_sequence

Logical, use the sequence-derived ORFs of transcript_orfs() when the annotation has sequences (default TRUE).

use_evidence

Logical, apply the evidence columns (default TRUE).

coding_cutoff

Coding probability below which a longest ORF (one that could not be projected from the canonical start) is not believed (default 0.364).

...

Passed on to methods or to fgsea::fgseaMultilevel().

group

Name of a col_data column defining groups; NULL for per-sample values.

levels

Order of the group levels; the change is last - first. For the tests (test_productive_fraction(), test_apa()), the two groups to compare; samples of other groups are ignored.

assay

Transcript assay to use (default "abundance"; "counts" for the test).

include_altered

Logical, count altered_productive isoforms as productive in productive_fraction() (default TRUE).

as_matrix

Logical, return the genes x samples matrix of productive fractions instead of the summary table.

min_expr

Minimum assay value for an isoform to contribute (default 0): isoforms below it count as zero.

inf_reps

Optional list of transcript matrices (inferential replicates with the same dimnames as the assay); NULL uses metadata(x)$inf_reps when present.

reference

Optional tibble from gtex_reference(), or a GTEx tissue name, giving the healthy-tissue productive fraction per gene.

genesets_list

Named list of gene symbol vectors (see read_gmt()).

min_size, max_size

Gene set size limits passed to fgsea.

Value

Tibbles, a matrix for productive_fraction(as_matrix = TRUE), a named character vector for productivity_palette(), a list with summary and confusion tibbles for benchmark_productivity().

Examples

iso <- example_isoformic()
prod <- transcript_productivity(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ")
#> Warning: ! 1 transcript has a sequence length differing from the exon length; its ORF is
#>   skipped.
prod[, c("transcript_name", "transcript_type", "productivity", "reason", "source")]
#> # A tibble: 10 × 5
#>    transcript_name transcript_type productivity       reason              source
#>    <chr>           <chr>           <fct>              <chr>               <chr> 
#>  1 RBPJ-222        protein_coding  uncertain          incomplete 3' end,… seque…
#>  2 RBPJ-201        protein_coding  productive         complete ORF ident… seque…
#>  3 RBPJ-206        protein_coding  productive         complete ORF ident… seque…
#>  4 RBPJ-225        retained_intron unproductive       unproductive bioty… annot…
#>  5 RBPJ-204        protein_coding  altered_productive alternative start … seque…
#>  6 RBPJ-205        protein_coding  altered_productive alternative start … seque…
#>  7 RBPJ-214        protein_coding  altered_productive alternative start … seque…
#>  8 RBPJ-208        protein_coding  altered_productive alternative start … seque…
#>  9 RBPJ-202        protein_coding  altered_productive alternative start … seque…
#> 10 RBPJ-210        retained_intron unproductive       unproductive bioty… annot…
